title: Russian forces take control of Kherson
body:
On 2 March 2022, one week after the start of the full-scale invasion, Russian forces took the Black Sea port city of Kherson in southern Ukraine. Local officials confirmed that Russian troops had entered the city, which was described as the first major urban centre to fall since the invasion began. The Russian army announced the seizure that morning. Kherson lies near Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014.

Gennady Lakhuta, head of the regional administration, wrote on Telegram that Russian troops were present throughout the city and posed serious danger. Mayor Igor Kolykhaiev, whose city had about 290,000 residents, said talks were under way with "armed guests" in the city administration. He said the city had no weapons and had not acted aggressively, that he had made no commitments to the invaders, and that he had asked them not to shoot civilians. He announced a night curfew and limits on car traffic and said the Ukrainian flag still flew over the city.

Reports from the same period said Berdiansk had also been seized, while Mariupol was reported to be repelling attacks and to be suffering shelling that left residents without power, water or heat. Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, had been bombarded. The article reported hundreds of civilian deaths and roughly one million people having fled Ukraine since the invasion began.
